market_outlook: This is a company-specific earnings note with no broad market directional commentary from Adam. No bull/bear lean on the overall market is expressed.

company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates ($56.05 vs. $54.03 expected), but the quality of the beat is low — roughly 250 basis points of gross margin tailwind came from tariff refunds and a non-cash LIFO benefit. Domestic comps disappointed at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex as a stronger player in the fast-growing Physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll posted solid FQ1 EPS upside at 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind (adjusted EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus). Sales missed, falling 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus $943.2 million expected, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed slightly but EPS guidance was held unchanged, and FQ2 EPS guidance midpoint of 46 cents is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings extensive CFO experience from Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership change with no financial results attached.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS estimates (78 cents vs. 87 cents expected) as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the Street's 13.85% estimate, pressured by rising material costs. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure on household budgets as headwinds, and expects a relatively flat retail sales environment in fiscal 2027 without providing formal guidance yet. Bright spots include healthy dealer inventory levels, ongoing structural cost reduction actions, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. This is a significant data readout in the highly competitive obesity drug space. The results reinforce Viking as a credible player in the GLP-1 market alongside larger incumbents.

sectors: RV/recreational vehicle sector faces headwinds per THOR Industries commentary — stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation are suppressing retail demand. Physical AI and robotics perception is a theme highlighted by the Cognex/RealSense deal. GLP-1 obesity drug space remains a high-focus area with Viking's positive trial data.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, so there's no broad macro or index commentary today — just the individual movers you need to know heading into the open.

Let's start with the most exciting name: Viking Therapeutics is spiking in pre-market after reporting positive trial results for its GLP-1 weight loss drug, showing 22% weight loss in participants. That's a big number in the obesity drug race and the market is rewarding it accordingly. Watch this one closely at the open.

AutoZone beat on earnings — $56.05 versus $54.03 expected — but don't get too excited about the quality. Roughly 250 basis points of gross margin help came from tariff refunds and a non-cash accounting item. Strip those out and the picture is murkier, especially with domestic comps coming in at plus 1.6% versus the Street's plus 3.1% expectation. The operating expense ratio also worsened. Management says sales improved in the back half of the quarter and they feel well-positioned for fiscal 2027, but this is a low-quality beat.

MillerKnoll is the better earnings story this morning. They posted 53 cents versus 36 cents expected, and here's the key — even backing out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still beat at 42 cents. Sales were light at $923 million versus $943 million expected, but orders grew 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year EPS guidance was held unchanged. This one looks more credible.

Cognex is making a move in Physical AI and robotics, announcing the acquisition of RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception — for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106 million. RealSense is growing revenue more than 50% year-over-year. This is a strategic bet on the Physical AI buildout theme.

THOR Industries missed on the bottom line, 78 cents versus 87 cents expected, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year. Management was candid about the tough backdrop — rates, fuel costs, and inflation are keeping retail soft. They won't give formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. The one silver lining is a 75% surge in North American towable RV order backlog, suggesting some pent-up demand.

Finally, Pentair named a new CFO, Bob Hau, effective November 1st. He comes from Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox — solid pedigree, but no financial results to trade off today.

Bottom line: Viking is the high-momentum name to watch. AutoZone beat looks optically better than it is. MillerKnoll is the clean beat. THOR is a miss with cautious tone. Position accordingly.
